newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka navy says two rebel Tiger boats damaged.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka navy says two rebel Tiger boats damaged.

text.p: Two Tamil Tiger guerrilla boats were damaged in a clash with Sri Lankan navy patrols off the island's northern coast early on Wednesday, a military statement said.

It said 12 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) boats were detected moving near Karathivu island, off northern Jaffna peninsula, some 380 km (237 miles) north of the capital Colombo and were engaged by naval patrols.
The statement said no naval personnel were injured and none of its vessels damaged in the attack, but it gave no details on Tiger casualties or how many navy vessels were involved.
The navy has stepped up attacks in recent weeks against the LTTE's naval Sea Tiger wing.
On Tuesday, the navy sank a rebel boat off the island's east coast and killed at least five guerrillas.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
